root.description: Section types shared by every kind of document, grouped by domain. A section is tagged group first, then leaf, without knowing the document's type; the doc-type rules then use the tags to decide or narrow the type.

nodes.label: General
nodes.description: Parts that any kind of document can have, such as front matter, summary, introduction, background, main body, findings, recommendations, conclusion, references and appendix, when no domain-specific group fits the section better.

children.label: Front matter
children.description: Material that precedes the main content, such as title page, table of contents, preface, copyright notices, list of figures, and a presentation's agenda.

children.label: Summary
children.description: A condensed statement of the key points of the whole document, such as an executive summary or overview; a scholarly paper's abstract belongs to research.abstract.

children.label: Introduction
children.description: The opening section that states the purpose, context, and scope of the document, or motivates a paper's problem and states its research questions or contributions.

children.label: Background
children.description: Context the reader needs before the main content, such as history, prior events, the problem setting, definitions, notation, or technical preliminaries, distinct from a review of competing work (research.related_work); the background of a court's opinion belongs to law.opinion.

children.label: Body
children.description: The substantive main content of the document that is neither introductory, concluding, nor back matter, when no more specific leaf in any group fits it.

children.label: Findings
children.description: The key findings drawn from a review, audit, investigation, survey or analysis, stated as the outcome of the work; the measured results of a scholarly paper's experiments belong to research.results and the actions proposed in response to general.recommendations.

children.label: Recommendations
children.description: Specific actions the authors recommend to a named audience, such as policy options, recommendations for executive action, or matters for a legislature to consider; a general wrap-up of the document belongs to general.conclusion.

children.label: Conclusion
children.description: The closing section that sums up what the document showed or argued, with next steps or future directions; specific recommended actions belong to general.recommendations.

children.label: Acknowledgments
children.description: Thanks to funders, colleagues, and reviewers, including funding statements and author contributions.

children.label: References
children.description: Bibliography, citations, footnotes, and links to sources used by the document; a standard's normative and informative references belong to standard.normative_references.

children.label: Appendix
children.description: Supplementary material placed after the main body, such as extra data, tables, proofs, derivations, additional experiments, forms, glossaries, indexes, and revision history, as opposed to the lookup material in technical.reference.

children.label: Other
children.description: Brief or administrative content that fits none of the other general parts, such as contact details, author biographies, disclaimers, legal notices, and colophons; substantive main text belongs to general.body.

nodes.label: Research
nodes.description: Sections specific to scholarly research papers: the abstract, the review of related work, methods, experiments, results, discussion, and limitations.

children.label: Abstract
children.description: A short self-contained summary of the problem, approach, and main findings placed at the start of the paper.

children.label: Related work
children.description: A survey of prior literature that positions the paper against existing approaches.

children.label: Method
children.description: The description of the proposed approach, model, algorithm, or study design, including how data were collected or processed.

children.label: Experiments
children.description: The experimental setup: datasets, baselines, metrics, implementation details, and evaluation protocol, before the numbers are discussed.

children.label: Results
children.description: The reported measurements and findings of the experiments or analyses, presented in tables and figures, without broader interpretation (which belongs to discussion).

children.label: Discussion
children.description: The interpretation of the results: their implications, possible explanations, and comparisons with prior work or expectations, rather than the reported numbers themselves (research.results); a court's discussion of the issues belongs to law.opinion.

children.label: Limitations
children.description: An explicit statement of the weaknesses, assumptions, threats to validity, and scope boundaries of the work.

children.label: Other
children.description: Research-paper content that fits none of the other research leaves, such as ethics statements, data and code availability, reproducibility checklists, and conflict-of-interest declarations; funding and thanks belong to general.acknowledgements.

nodes.label: Management narrative
nodes.description: Management's own account of a company or fund in prose: letters to shareholders or investors, the business overview, management's discussion and analysis, and the outlook.

children.label: Shareholder or investor letter
children.description: A narrative letter from the chairman, CEO, or fund manager to shareholders or investors that reviews the period and the outlook in the writer's own voice, as opposed to the formal business overview or MD&A sections.
examples: Letter from the Chief Executive Officer

children.label: Business overview
children.description: A description of what the company does, its products, markets, competition, customers, and strategy (Form 10-K Item 1).

children.label: Management discussion and analysis
children.description: Management's narrative explanation of results of operations, liquidity, capital resources, and trends, including market-risk disclosures (MD&A, Items 7 and 7A).
examples: Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk

children.label: Outlook
children.description: Management's forward-looking view of the coming period, such as financial guidance, targets, expected market conditions, and priorities; a review of the period just ended belongs to narrative.management_discussion, and the legal caution about forward-looking statements to disclosure.forward_looking_statements.

children.label: Other
children.description: Narrative content about the company or fund that fits none of the other narrative leaves, such as company history, case studies, and customer stories; a letter addressed to shareholders or investors belongs to narrative.shareholder_letter.

nodes.label: Financial statements
nodes.description: Financial statements and the material that accompanies them: the primary statements, a fund's schedule of investments, the notes, the auditor's report, financial highlights, and statements of a customer's account.

children.label: Financial statements
children.description: A section that presents the primary financial statements together as a set under one heading, such as Item 8 of a Form 10-K or the condensed statements of a 10-Q; a section holding a single statement belongs to that statement's leaf, and the notes and the auditor's report have leaves of their own.
examples: Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data

children.label: Balance sheet
children.description: The statement of financial position at a date, listing assets, liabilities, and equity, or a fund's statement of assets and liabilities or of net assets; not the income statement, which covers a period.

children.label: Income statement
children.description: The statement of revenues, expenses, and profit or loss for a period, including earnings per share and comprehensive income, or a fund's statement of operations; not management's narrative about those results (narrative.management_discussion) or the line-item detail in the notes.

children.label: Cash-flow statement
children.description: The statement of cash flows for a period, splitting the cash generated and used into operating, investing, and financing activities; not the liquidity discussion in narrative.management_discussion.
examples: Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows

children.label: Statement of changes in equity
children.description: The statement of changes in shareholders' equity or, for a fund, in net assets, reconciling opening to closing equity through income, dividends, share issues, and buybacks; not the equity section of the balance sheet at a single date.
examples: Statement of Changes in Net Assets
Statement of Changes in Shareholders' Equity

children.label: Schedule of investments
children.description: The complete list of a fund's or investment company's positions at a date, with quantities, costs, and fair values, as part of its financial statements; not a summary of top holdings or allocations (fund.holdings_and_allocation).

children.label: Auditor's report
children.description: The independent auditor's or accountant's report giving an opinion on, or the results of a review of, the financial statements or internal control, including critical or key audit matters; not management's own report on internal control (disclosure.controls_and_procedures).
examples: Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm
Report on Review of Interim Financial Information

children.label: Notes to financial statements
children.description: The numbered explanatory notes on accounting policies, estimates, and line-item detail that accompany and support the financial statements.
examples: Note 1. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies

children.label: Account statement
children.description: A statement of one customer's account for a period, such as a bank, brokerage, retirement, or insurance account, with that account's balance, transactions, holdings, and fees; not a company's or fund's own financial statements.

children.label: Financial highlights
children.description: A short summary of headline figures for the period, such as key figures, selected financial data, the results table on a release's first page, or a fund's per-share financial highlights; the full statements belong to their own leaves.

children.label: Other
children.description: Financial material that fits none of the other financial leaves, such as non-GAAP reconciliations, segment tables, and supplementary or unaudited financial data; narrative about the results belongs to narrative.management_discussion.

nodes.label: Corporate disclosures
nodes.description: Regulatory and corporate disclosures of a company's filings and shareholder documents: risk factors, governance, executive pay, shareholder-meeting proposals, controls, legal proceedings, properties, the market for its stock, forward-looking-statement legends, and exhibit lists.

children.label: Risk factors
children.description: A discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could materially harm the business, a fund, or the value of the securities, such as the risk factors of a filing or offering document and a fund's principal risks (market, credit, interest-rate, liquidity); not the strategy that gives rise to them (fund.principal_investment_strategies).
examples: Principal Risks of Investing in the Fund

children.label: Corporate governance
children.description: Information about the board of directors, its committees, director independence, officers, and governance practices and policies.
examples: Item 10. Directors, Executive Officers and Corporate Governance

children.label: Executive compensation
children.description: Disclosure of pay for senior executives and directors, including salary, bonuses, equity awards, and pay-versus-performance tables.

children.label: Shareholder meeting and proposals
children.description: The notice and logistics of a shareholder meeting and the proposals to be voted on, such as voting procedures, proxy solicitation, quorum, and each proposal with the board's recommendation; the nominees' biographies belong to disclosure.corporate_governance and the pay tables to disclosure.executive_compensation.
examples: Notice of Annual Meeting of Shareholders
Questions and Answers About the Annual Meeting and Voting
Ratification of Appointment of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm
Advisory Vote to Approve Executive Compensation

children.label: Controls and procedures
children.description: Management's evaluation of disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting, including any material weaknesses (Item 9A).
examples: Management's Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting
Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting

children.label: Legal proceedings
children.description: A description of pending or threatened litigation, regulatory actions, and other legal matters involving the company (Item 3).

children.label: Properties
children.description: A description of the company's principal physical facilities, such as plants, offices, and real estate it owns or leases (Item 2).

children.label: Market for equity
children.description: Information on the market for the company's common stock, including listing, holders, dividends, share repurchases, and stock performance (Item 5).
examples: Item 5. Market for Registrant's Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities

children.label: Forward-looking statements
children.description: The legal legend cautioning that forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties, often naming the factors and claiming a safe harbor, and similar important-notice disclaimers of investor documents; the outlook itself belongs to narrative.outlook and the risks themselves to disclosure.risk_factors.

children.label: Exhibits
children.description: The list of exhibits and filed documents, signatures, and schedules incorporated by reference in a regulatory filing, which carries no narrative content of its own (Item 15); the signature blocks and attachments of an agreement belong to contract.signatures_exhibits.
examples: Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules

children.label: Other
children.description: Disclosure material that fits none of the other disclosure leaves, such as mine safety, cybersecurity, auditor fees, related-party transactions, and unresolved staff comments; a filing's cover page and table of contents belong to general.front_matter.

nodes.label: Sustainability and ESG
nodes.description: Sustainability and ESG reporting: the overall sustainability approach, environmental and climate topics, social and workforce topics, and ESG data tables and framework indexes.

children.label: Sustainability
children.description: A company's overall approach to sustainability, such as its strategy, materiality assessment, ESG governance, commitments, and stakeholder engagement, when no single environmental or social topic is the subject; board and corporate governance in general belongs to disclosure.corporate_governance.

children.label: Climate and environment
children.description: Environmental topics such as climate strategy and risks, greenhouse-gas emissions, energy, water, waste, biodiversity, and climate-related financial disclosures; social topics belong to esg.social.

children.label: Social and workforce
children.description: Social topics such as workforce and human capital, diversity and inclusion, health and safety, human rights, labor in the supply chain, and communities and philanthropy; board governance belongs to disclosure.corporate_governance.

children.label: ESG data and indexes
children.description: ESG data tables and the indexes that map disclosures to GRI, SASB, TCFD, or other frameworks, together with assurance statements on them; narrative about a topic belongs to that topic's leaf.

children.label: Other
children.description: Sustainability content that fits none of the other ESG leaves, such as product responsibility, responsible-investment policies, awards, and memberships; the overall approach belongs to esg.sustainability.

nodes.label: Fund
nodes.description: Sections that describe an investment fund or share class to investors: objective, strategies, fees, performance, holdings, key facts, management, buying and selling shares, and taxes.

children.label: Investment objective
children.description: The fund's stated investment goal, such as long-term capital growth, current income, or tracking an index, usually in one or two sentences; how the fund pursues that goal belongs to fund.principal_investment_strategies.

children.label: Principal investment strategies
children.description: How the fund pursues its objective: the kinds of securities it buys, its selection process or index methodology, and limits on what it may hold; not the risks of those investments (disclosure.risk_factors) or the portfolio held on a given date (fund.holdings_and_allocation).
examples: Principal Investment Strategies of the Fund

children.label: Fees and expenses
children.description: The costs of buying, holding, and selling fund shares: shareholder fees and sales charges, annual operating expenses and expense ratios, fee waivers, the expense example, and portfolio turnover.
examples: Fees and Expenses of the Fund

children.label: Performance
children.description: Past returns of the fund or share class and its benchmark: annual return bar charts, average annual total return tables, best and worst quarters, the growth of a hypothetical investment, and commentary on past results; not the fund's costs (fund.fees_and_expenses).

children.label: Holdings and allocation
children.description: What the fund holds as of a date: its top holdings, the number of holdings, and breakdowns by asset class, sector, region, credit quality, or maturity; not the strategy that selects them (fund.principal_investment_strategies) or the complete audited list of positions (financial.schedule_of_investments).

children.label: Fund facts
children.description: The key-facts block that identifies a fund or share class, such as tickers and other identifiers, inception date, net assets, benchmark, share classes, and distribution frequency; a key-facts expense ratio belongs to fund.fees_and_expenses and the number of holdings to fund.holdings_and_allocation.

children.label: Management
children.description: Who runs the fund: the investment adviser and any sub-advisers, the portfolio managers with their tenure and experience, and the management company; the fees paid to them belong to fund.fees_and_expenses, and an operating company's directors and officers to disclosure.corporate_governance.

children.label: Purchase and sale
children.description: How investors buy, sell, exchange, or redeem shares: minimum investments, available share classes, how orders are placed and priced, and exchange trading; the charges on those transactions belong to fund.fees_and_expenses.
examples: Purchase and Sale of Fund Shares

children.label: Tax information
children.description: How the fund's distributions and the sale of its shares are taxed, together with its dividend and capital gain distribution policy; distribution rates and yields as measures of return belong to fund.performance.

children.label: Other
children.description: Fund content that fits none of the other fund leaves, such as payments to financial intermediaries, service providers, shareholder services, and legal notices; a fund document's cover page and table of contents belong to general.front_matter.
examples: Payments to Broker-Dealers and Other Financial Intermediaries

nodes.label: Securities offering
nodes.description: Sections of an offering document for newly issued securities, such as an IPO or bond prospectus: the terms of the offering, the use of proceeds, capitalization and dilution, and underwriting.

children.label: Offering terms
children.description: The terms of the securities being offered and of the offering itself, such as the summary of the offering, the description of the shares or notes, pricing, and the timetable; how the money raised will be used belongs to offering.use_of_proceeds.

children.label: Use of proceeds
children.description: How the issuer intends to use the money raised by the offering; not the issuer's business strategy in general (narrative.business_overview).
examples: Reasons for the Offer and Use of Proceeds

children.label: Capitalization and dilution
children.description: The issuer's capitalization and indebtedness before and after the offering and the dilution new investors suffer; not the balance sheet itself (financial.balance_sheet).

children.label: Underwriting
children.description: How the securities are sold: the underwriters or placement agents, their commitments and discounts, lock-ups, stabilization, and the plan of distribution; the fees an investor pays to a fund belong to fund.fees_and_expenses.

children.label: Other
children.description: Offering content that fits none of the other offering leaves, such as the experts, the validity of the securities, shares eligible for future sale, and where to find more information; the issuer's risks belong to disclosure.risk_factors.
examples: Where You Can Find More Information

nodes.label: Contract and terms
nodes.description: Clauses of agreements between named parties and of published terms of service and policies: parties, definitions, obligations, payment, intellectual property, warranties, liability, termination, disputes, privacy, acceptable use, and signatures.

children.label: Parties and recitals
children.description: The preamble that names the contracting parties, the effective date, and the background recitals (the whereas clauses) that explain the purpose.

children.label: Definitions
children.description: Clauses that define capitalized terms and rules of interpretation used throughout the agreement; a standard's terms and definitions belong to standard.terminology.

children.label: Scope and services
children.description: The clauses describing the work, services, products, or deliverables that a party is to provide and the standards for providing them.

children.label: Term
children.description: The clauses fixing the duration of the agreement, its effective period, and renewal or extension mechanics.

children.label: Payment
children.description: The clauses on fees, prices, invoicing, payment timing, expenses, taxes, and late-payment consequences.

children.label: Confidentiality
children.description: The clauses obliging the parties to protect each other's non-public information and limiting its use and disclosure.

children.label: Intellectual property
children.description: The clauses on ownership and assignment of, and licenses to, intellectual property such as inventions, work product, trademarks, and software.

children.label: Warranties
children.description: The clauses in which parties represent facts and promise quality or performance standards, together with disclaimers of other warranties.

children.label: Indemnification
children.description: The clauses requiring one party to compensate the other for specified third-party claims, losses, or damages.

children.label: Limitation of liability
children.description: The clauses capping or excluding damages and defining which types of loss each party cannot recover.

children.label: Termination
children.description: The clauses stating how and when either party may end the agreement early, for cause or convenience, and what happens afterwards.

children.label: Governing law and disputes
children.description: The clauses selecting the governing law, jurisdiction or venue, and dispute-resolution method such as arbitration or mediation.

children.label: General provisions
children.description: Boilerplate clauses such as notices, assignment, amendment, severability, entire agreement, force majeure, and counterparts.

children.label: Signatures and exhibits
children.description: The signature blocks and the attached schedules, exhibits, or annexes that complete the agreement.

children.label: Privacy and personal data
children.description: The terms on collecting, using, sharing, retaining, and protecting personal data and cookies, and the rights users have over their data, as in a privacy policy or data-processing terms; the parties' duty to protect each other's business secrets belongs to contract.confidentiality.

children.label: Acceptable use
children.description: The rules on what users may and may not do with a published service, such as prohibited conduct and content, account rules, and the provider's enforcement; the work a party owes a named counterparty belongs to contract.scope_services.

children.label: Other
children.description: Clauses that fit none of the other contract leaves, such as non-competition, non-solicitation, insurance, audit rights, and employment benefits; boilerplate such as notices and assignment belongs to contract.general_provisions.

nodes.label: Court opinions and legislation
nodes.description: Parts of court opinions and of legislation: the case caption, the syllabus, the court's opinion, concurring and dissenting opinions, and a statute's or regulation's preamble, operative provisions, and amendments.

children.label: Case caption
children.description: The caption and docket block that identifies the court, the parties, the docket number, the dates argued and decided, and the judges or counsel; not the reporter's summary of the case (law.syllabus).
examples: Supreme Court of the United States
Appeal from the United States District Court

children.label: Syllabus
children.description: The headnote or syllabus that summarizes the case and its holdings, prepared by the court's reporter for the reader's convenience; the court's own reasoning belongs to law.opinion.

children.label: Opinion of the court
children.description: The court's own opinion: the facts and procedural history as the court recites them, its legal analysis, holding, and disposition, whether for a majority, per curiam, or by a single judge, including the background, discussion, and conclusion sections it is divided into; a separate concurrence or dissent belongs to law.separate_opinion.

children.label: Concurring or dissenting opinion
children.description: A concurring or dissenting opinion written separately by one or more judges, agreeing or disagreeing with the court's judgment or reasoning; the opinion for the court belongs to law.opinion.
examples: Concurring in Part and Dissenting in Part

children.label: Title and enactment
children.description: The opening of a statute, bill, regulation, or treaty: its long and short titles, the recitals of a regulation, the enacting clause, and statements of findings or purposes; the operative rules belong to law.provisions.

children.label: Statutory provisions
children.description: The operative provisions of a statute, bill, regulation, or treaty, arranged as titles, parts, articles, sections, and subsections that state the legal rules; changes made to other laws belong to law.amendments.

children.label: Amendments to law
children.description: Provisions that amend, repeal, or conform other laws or earlier versions of the same law; the new law's own rules belong to law.provisions.

children.label: Other
children.description: Legal content that fits none of the other law leaves, such as effective dates, transitional and savings provisions, authorizations of appropriations, and appendices to an opinion; contract boilerplate belongs to contract.general_provisions.

nodes.label: Product documentation
nodes.description: Documentation of a hardware or software product: overview, installation, configuration, usage, reference, specifications, pins and interfaces, package data, ordering information, safety, and troubleshooting.

children.label: Overview
children.description: A high-level introduction to what the product or system is, its features, purpose, and intended audience.

children.label: Installation and getting started
children.description: Instructions for installing, setting up, or first running the product, including requirements and quick-start steps.

children.label: Configuration
children.description: Explanation of settings, options, parameters, and environment needed to tailor the product's behavior.

children.label: Usage
children.description: Task-oriented instructions and examples showing how to operate the product in normal use, including a datasheet's typical application circuits.

children.label: Reference
children.description: Lookup material such as API, command, register, message, or function descriptions, organized for consultation rather than reading in order.

children.label: Specifications
children.description: Quantitative technical data such as electrical characteristics, ratings, dimensions, timing, and performance limits, typically in tables.

children.label: Pins and interfaces
children.description: Descriptions of a product's pins, ports, connectors, signals, and buses, with pinout diagrams and pin-function tables; their electrical limits belong to technical.specifications and register maps to technical.reference.

children.label: Package and mechanical data
children.description: Package and mechanical information such as package outline drawings, footprints and land patterns, marking, and tape-and-reel details; tabulated ratings and dimensions of the product belong to technical.specifications.

children.label: Ordering information
children.description: How to order the product: part numbers and their coding, variants, order codes, available packages, accessories, and kits; the prices and payment terms of a sale belong to contract.payment.

children.label: Safety and compliance
children.description: Safety instructions, warnings, and cautions, and regulatory compliance statements such as FCC, CE, or UL notices; the procedures for normal use belong to technical.usage.

children.label: Troubleshooting
children.description: Guidance on diagnosing problems, including error messages, symptoms, causes, fixes, and frequently asked questions.

children.label: Other
children.description: Product documentation that fits none of the other technical leaves, such as warranty and support information, release notes, and disposal; diagnosing errors belongs to technical.troubleshooting.

nodes.label: Technical standard
nodes.description: Sections specific to normative technical standards and protocol specifications, such as RFCs and ISO, IEEE, or W3C documents: scope, terminology and requirements language, the normative specification, conformance, security and registry considerations, and normative references.

children.label: Scope
children.description: The normative statement of what a standard covers, what it applies to, and what it leaves out; a general introduction or motivation belongs to general.introduction.

children.label: Terminology and conventions
children.description: The terms, definitions, symbols, and abbreviations a standard uses, and its requirements language, such as the BCP 14 key words MUST and SHOULD; an agreement's defined terms belong to contract.definitions.

children.label: Normative specification
children.description: The normative body of a standard that precisely defines a protocol, format, data model, algorithm, or interface for implementers, using requirement key words; a vendor's user-facing API reference belongs to technical.reference.

children.label: Conformance
children.description: The conditions an implementation must meet to claim conformance, such as conformance classes, levels, profiles, and test criteria; the requirements themselves belong to standard.specification.

children.label: Security considerations
children.description: The analysis of the security and privacy threats, attacks, and mitigations that implementers of the standard must consider; a product's safety warnings belong to technical.safety.

children.label: Registry considerations
children.description: Instructions to a registry authority such as IANA to create or update the registries, code points, media types, or other identifiers the standard defines; what the identifiers mean belongs to standard.specification.

children.label: Normative references
children.description: The lists of documents a standard cites, split into normative references needed to implement it and informative references for background; a general bibliography belongs to general.references.

children.label: Other
children.description: Standards material that fits none of the other standard leaves, such as the document status, changes from previous versions, implementation status, contributors, and authors' addresses; the title page and copyright notice belong to general.front_matter.
